subject: Next steps — Luminova procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO)
messages:
From: Maya Shah <maya.shah@luminova.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Rao <prao@luminova.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement questions

Thanks for the call today — really helpful. A couple of items I promised to confirm internally and share here so we can agree next steps: 

1) Payment preference: Luminova procurement typically goes via a PO routed through our central FinOps team. We *can* use card for initial POC spend (<$5k) but anything above that needs a PO.

2) Marketplace vs direct purchase: Our procurement lead prefers marketplace purchases where possible because it simplifies the finance/renewal flow and avoids vendor onboarding. That said, if pricing or contract terms aren’t available in the marketplace, they will default to a PO.

3) Timing: FinOps says typical internal PO cycle is ~3 weeks for an established vendor (vendor onboarding + legal review) but could stretch to 6 weeks for something new.

Action items from our side: can you send a short checklist of what Redwood needs for marketplace listing (pricing SKU, billing contact, technical lead) and a clean pricing sheet we can attach to the request? Also, please confirm whether Redwood supports invoiced billing via PO for Dedicated/Private plans.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Luminova AI
maya.shah@luminova.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 17:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps — Luminova procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Hi Maya — great to meet you and thanks for the clear summary. High level answers below, plus I’ve attached a concise pricing sheet and a procurement checklist that others have used with marketplace teams.

Quick answers:
- Marketplace support: Yes — we publish in AWS Marketplace and can enable GCP Marketplace on request. Azure marketplace is on our roadmap this quarter; we can discuss timelines if that's preferred.
- PO/invoiced billing: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments (and Enterprise-tier hosted agreements). We can accept POs and issue monthly invoices.
- Minimums: For invoiced billing we typically require an initial commitment (monthly or annual) depending on the product. Details on the sheet.
- Marketplace SKUs: included in the attached pricing sheet (columns: sku, tier, monthly tokens, list price).

Requested next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll loop in Ben (billing) and Karthik (marketplace enablement) to confirm onboarding checklist and any one-off marketplace requirements.
- Ben will send the vendor onboarding packet and sample SOW if needed.

If it helps, I can be on a short call with your FinOps to walk through the checklist — happy to schedule for Wed/Thu this week.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123

Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps — Luminova procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Hi Maya / Priyanka — Ben here from Billing. Quick notes and what I need to move forward: 

What we can do now:
- Accept PO and invoice monthly for Enterprise/Dedicated usage.
- Support card billing for POC under $5k.
- Provide required vendor onboarding details (W9, tax info, contact for billing).

What we need from Luminova to start vendor onboarding:
- Name and email of the person who will sign the PO (or confirmation that signatory is in-house).
- Vendor onboarding form filled (I attached a one-page example to this email).
- Expected start date and estimated monthly spend for first 3 months.

Marketplace note from Karthik (cc’d): depending on whether you want the AWS Marketplace listing to cover a committed Reserved plan or a standard metered listing, the billing flow differs. If you want the reserved/commit model in marketplace, that requires an extra step on our side (partner registration) and typically 2–3 weeks to publish. Metered listing is faster (3–5 business days) but will not provide the same contract semantics.

I’m available for a 30-minute call with your procurement on Wednesday 13th at 10am PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: vendor-onboarding-example.pdf
From: Priyanka Rao <prao@luminova.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Maya Shah <maya.shah@luminova.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps — Luminova procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Thanks everyone — Wednesday 10am PT works for our procurement lead (Ishaan Verma) and me. A couple clarifications from our side before the call: 

- We prefer marketplace reserved/commit if Redwood can publish a reserved SKU that maps to an annual commitment. That is our preferred flow for predictable spend and easier renewals.
- For the PO path: our typical PO approval requires a short vendor questionnaire filled out by vendor security (SOC2 status, data residency, logging). Can Ben or Karthik confirm who owns the security questionnaire responses?
- Expected target go-live for POC is Sep 1st; if marketplace reserved listing will take 2–3 weeks to publish then we might need to start with a card-pay POC and convert to marketplace reserved later.

Ishaan will join the call; I’ll send a calendar invite and attach our vendor questionnaire.

Best,
Priyanka Rao
Sourcing Manager, Luminova AI
prao@luminova.ai
